BiblicalUsage: God tells Sennacherib He will put His bridle in his lips and turn him back by the way he came, and Isaiah repeats the word to the same king. The bit is God's restraint on a raging power, and the verse is a promise that no enemy runs loose beyond God's hand.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the bridle is one of Scripture's kindest pictures of sovereignty: even the proudest king is steered, and God turns him home by the road he came.
